🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>China to the US Ambassador: Stop Trying to Sow Discord With Mexico</u>

At the Milken conference in Mexico City on October 28, US Ambassador Ronald Johnson claimed China would benefit from Mexico being "a chaotic and insecure place" on the US southern border. China's embassy answered with "strong discontent and categorical rejection," calling the idea that China loves chaos "pure invention and malicious slander." It said Beijing always supports Mexico's efforts to defend its sovereignty and security, and pointed at what actually fuels the violence: US guns and drug money.
banner: CHINA TO US ENVOY: STOP SOWING DISCORD

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Inés Gómez Mont Arrested in Florida After Five Years on the Run</u>

US authorities arrested the former TV host in Florida. She and her husband, Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga, the so-called "King of the Invoice Mills," have faced Mexican arrest warrants since 2021 for money laundering, organized crime and embezzlement. Prosecutors link them to a web of shell companies billing fake services that drained about 3 billion pesos from the Interior Ministry under Peña Nieto. In September Interpol dropped their red notices; Sheinbaum objected that there was proof they invoiced businessmen "with fake invoices to avoid paying taxes." Mexico now has to request her extradition.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE Comptroller: 5 Companies and 13 People Rigged Electoral-Supply Contracts Worth 2.46 Billion Pesos</u>

Before Congress on October 30, the INE's internal comptroller, Víctor Hugo Carvente, laid out the network behind Mexico's electoral materials: five companies and at least 13 individuals sharing shareholders, legal reps and proxies, who won 2,461 million pesos in contracts between 2014 and 2024. That is all of Lorenzo Córdova's tenure plus Taddei's first two years. Formas Finas alone got 778.7 million under Córdova; Cajas Graf, 915.5 million. The comptroller's finding: "collusion in tenders that generates overpricing, restricts effective competition" and displaces other suppliers.

🇲🇽🌲 <u>Tlahuica People Near a Ruling on 18,000 Hectares of Ancestral Forest</u>

The Tlahuica Pjiekakjoo community of San Juan Atzingo, in Ocuilan, State of Mexico, expects the Superior Agrarian Court to rule soon on more than 18,000 hectares of communal forest. Their land was titled in 2007, then challenged from 2014 by neighbors with real-estate and logging interests. Last year a lower agrarian court annulled their title. Now the federal Agrarian Prosecutor, Víctor Suárez, has filed an amicus brief backed by an INAH expert report: the Tlahuica have been on this land for more than 3,000 years.

🇲🇽🪖 <u>Plan DN-III-E Turns 60: 87,000 Emergencies Answered</u>

Since June 1966, Mexico's Army has run Plan DN-III-E, its disaster-relief plan, in more than 87,000 emergencies: floods, earthquakes, hurricanes, search and rescue. At the 60th-anniversary ceremony at AIFA on October 30, Sheinbaum and General Ricardo Trevilla awarded 869 decorations to Army, Air Force and National Guard personnel. Sheinbaum thanked the troops "for searching, for rescuing and for not leaving Mexican families alone," and said their greatness lies "in their human quality, their vocation of service and their commitment to the Mexican people."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex Refining Hits Its Highest Level Since 2014</u>

Mexico's national refining system processed 1.143 million barrels a day in Q3, up 13.8% from a year earlier and the most since 2014, El Financiero reports. Gasoline output rose 15.9% and diesel 23.3%. Revenue climbed 28.5% to 487 billion pesos, and financial debt fell to $77.6 billion, more than $28 billion lower than in 2018.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Sheinbaum Opens Mercado Libre's First Robotic Hub in Mexico: $600M, 4,700 Jobs</u>

The distribution center in Villa de Tezontepec, Hidalgo, is part of Plan México. It's a $600 million-plus investment that opened with 240 robots and is designed to scale up to 1,000. It employs more than 4,700 people directly and already moves 6.8 million packages a month. Sheinbaum said Mexico's big draw today is its engineers and skilled workforce, and tied the investment wave to wage gains since 2018.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Right-Wing Intellectuals Miss the "Democracy of the Chayote"</u>

Enrique Krauze went to Spain and told a crowd that Mexico is living through "dark times." Sheinbaum answered that what these intellectuals miss is the old arrangement of cheques, private dinners with the president and access to power. She traced Héctor Aguilar Camín's path from Salinas to Zedillo, Fox, Calderón and Peña Nieto, "because they all pampered him, and now he is against us." Then: "They were the owners of the word. Now it's the people."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>At COP17, Mexico Brings Its Own Conservation Agenda — and Asks for Real Money</u>

At COP17 of the Biodiversity Convention, governments pledged over $1.8 billion in new funding. Mexico showed up with MEx30x30 to protect 30% of its land and sea by 2030, along with Green Climate Fund and KfW-backed projects for its protected areas. Semarnat's Marina Robles: "Mexico has its own agenda to advance the conservation of its biodiversity. The challenge is ensuring that commitments translate into concrete actions, backed by sufficient, timely and accessible resources."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Texas Grabs 9 Islands in the Río Bravo. Mexico Points to the Treaty.</u>

Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham claimed nine islands between Laredo and McAllen and cleared state forces to patrol them, all to "maintain operational security." CBP had asked about 28 islands it called of uncertain ownership. Mexico's SRE answered that under the 1970 Boundary Treaty, the border follows the normal channel of the Río Bravo, and only the binational CILA can decide sovereignty.
